laws.title: Hands-Free Driving Law
laws.subtitle: IA Code §Traffic Code — No handheld devices while driving
laws.fullDescription: Iowa prohibits holding or using handheld electronic devices while driving. Handheld device ban while driving.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are exempt from hands-free requirements.

quiz.q: Is handheld phone use banned while driving in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: handheld device use while driving is prohibited.

laws.title: Non-Resident Hunting & Fishing License
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Fish & Game Code — Non-residents must purchase licenses
laws.fullDescription: Non-residents must obtain a valid Iowa hunting or fishing license before taking game or fish. Annual non-resident fishing licenses cost approximately $45; hunting licenses cost approximately $150. Some species require additional tags.
laws.penalty: Class A misdemeanor or felony; fines up to $1000 plus equipment forfeiture.
laws.exceptions: Residents are exempt from non-resident fees.

quiz.q: What is the penalty for hunting without a license in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Hunting without a license in Iowa is a Class A misdemeanor with fines up to $1000.

laws.title: Impaired Driving (DUI/DWI)
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Vehicle Code — 0.08% BAC limit
laws.fullDescription: Iowa prohibits operating a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Commercial drivers: 0.04%. Drivers under 21: 0.02 BAC. Implied consent laws apply.
laws.penalty: First offense: $500–$1,000 fine, license suspension, up to 1 year jail. Subsequent offenses carry mandatory minimums and longer suspensions.
laws.exceptions: None — even prescription medication impairment can result in DUI charges.

quiz.q: What BAC triggers a DUI in Iowa for regular drivers?
quiz.explanation: The legal BAC limit in Iowa is 0.08% for regular drivers, consistent with all US states.

laws.title: Open Container Law
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Vehicle Code — No open alcohol in vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Iowa prohibits open alcoholic beverage containers in the passenger area of motor vehicles on public roads. Open container law applies to driver and passengers.
laws.penalty: $250 fine; applies to driver and passengers.
laws.exceptions: Passengers in for-hire vehicles (taxis, limos) may be exempt.

quiz.q: Can passengers drink alcohol in a private car in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa's open container law applies to all vehicle occupants.

laws.title: Recreational Cannabis — Not Legal
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §124.401 — Recreational cannabis NOT legal
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Iowa has a very limited medical CBD program (Iowa Medical Cannabidiol Act) allowing only high-CBD oil for patients with severe epilepsy and other conditions. Recreational cannabis is illegal.
laws.penalty: Possession: misdemeanor to felony.
laws.exceptions: Medical patients exempt.

quiz.q: Is recreational cannabis legal in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Recreational cannabis not legal.

laws.title: Medical Cannabis — Legal
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §124E — Medical cannabis program
laws.fullDescription: Iowa has a very limited medical cannabidiol program — low-THC CBD oil only for qualifying patients.
laws.penalty: Non-patients face criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Registered patients are exempt from possession penalties.

quiz.q: Does Iowa have a medical cannabis program?
quiz.explanation: Iowa has a medical cannabis program.

laws.title: Firearm Carry Law — Constitutional
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §724.11 — Constitutional state
laws.fullDescription: Iowa is a constitutional state. Iowa changed from a may-issue to shall-issue permit system in 2021. Constitutional carry also enacted in 2021.
laws.penalty: Carrying while prohibited: felony.
laws.exceptions: Firearms prohibited in schools, courts, and government buildings.

quiz.q: What type of carry law does Iowa have?
quiz.explanation: Iowa has constitutional — permitless carry enacted in 2021

laws.title: Background Check Requirements
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §18 USC 922 — Federal NICS checks at licensed dealers
laws.fullDescription: All firearm purchases from licensed dealers in Iowa require a federal NICS background check. Private sales do not require background checks.
laws.penalty: Straw purchases or sales to prohibited persons: federal felony up to 10 years.
laws.exceptions: Transfers between immediate family members may be exempt.

quiz.q: Does Iowa require background checks for private gun sales?
quiz.explanation: Iowa only requires background checks for licensed dealer gun sales.

laws.title: Stand Your Ground / Castle Doctrine
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Criminal Code — Stand Your Ground
laws.fullDescription: Iowa has a Stand Your Ground law — no duty to retreat.
laws.penalty: N/A — this law provides a defense against criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Force not justified if defender is committing a crime or the intruder is a co-resident.

quiz.q: Does Iowa have a Stand Your Ground law?
options: No — duty to retreat outside home
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Stand Your Ground — no duty to retreat.

laws.title: Minimum Wage Law
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Labor Code — $7.25/hour minimum wage
laws.fullDescription: Iowa's minimum wage is $7.25/hour (2024). Iowa uses the federal minimum of $7.25/hr. State attempts to raise it have not passed.
laws.penalty: Employers violating minimum wage: back wages, double damages, and attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Tipped workers may have a lower base.

quiz.q: What is the minimum wage in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa's minimum wage is $7.25/hour.

laws.title: At-Will Employment
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Labor Code — Employment at will doctrine
laws.fullDescription: Iowa follows at-will employment. Employers may terminate for any legal reason; employees may quit anytime. at-will employment with standard exceptions.
laws.penalty: N/A — at-will is the default standard.
laws.exceptions: Termination for illegal reasons (discrimination, retaliation) is prohibited.

quiz.q: Can an Iowa employer fire an employee without giving a reason?
quiz.explanation: Iowa is an at-will employment state — employers may generally terminate without cause.

laws.title: Right-to-Work Law — Yes
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Labor Code — Iowa is a right-to-work state
laws.fullDescription: Iowa is a right-to-work state. Iowa is a right-to-work state (since 1947).
laws.penalty: N/A — this governs labor relations framework.
laws.exceptions: Federal employees and some categories are governed by federal law.

quiz.q: Is Iowa a right-to-work state?
quiz.explanation: Iowa is a right-to-work state.

laws.title: Non-Compete Agreement Enforceability
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Business Code — Non-compete enforceability rules
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Non-competes enforced if reasonable.
laws.penalty: Overly broad agreements may be voided or reformed by courts.
laws.exceptions: Agreements protecting legitimate trade secrets are most favored.

quiz.q: Are non-compete agreements automatically enforceable in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Courts assess reasonableness.

laws.title: Paid Sick Leave — Not Required
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Labor Code — No mandate
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: No statewide paid sick leave.
laws.penalty: N/A
laws.exceptions: Independent contractors are generally not covered.

quiz.q: Does Iowa require employers to provide paid sick leave?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: No paid sick leave mandate.

laws.title: Unemployment Insurance
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Labor Code — Unemployment benefits
laws.fullDescription: Iowa unemployment insurance provides benefits to eligible workers. Maximum weekly benefit: $400 for up to 26 weeks. Workers must have earned at least $1500 in the base period.
laws.penalty: Filing fraudulent claims: repayment plus penalties and possible criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Self-employed and independent contractors are generally ineligible for regular UI.

quiz.q: What is the maximum weekly unemployment benefit in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa's maximum weekly unemployment benefit is $400.

laws.title: Workers' Compensation
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Labor Code — Mandatory workers' comp coverage
laws.fullDescription: Iowa requires employers with 1 or more employees to carry workers' compensation insurance. Covers medical costs and lost wages for work-related injuries.
laws.penalty: Employers without coverage: fines up to $5000/day, personal liability for claims.
laws.exceptions: Sole proprietors and some domestic workers may be exempt.

quiz.q: How many employees trigger workers' comp requirements in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa requires workers' comp for employers with 1 or more employees.

laws.title: Independent Contractor Classification
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Labor Code — Worker classification rules
laws.fullDescription: Iowa uses Common law control test to classify workers. Worker classification uses common law control test.
laws.penalty: Misclassification: back taxes, penalties, and retroactive benefits liability.
laws.exceptions: Licensed professionals may have different classification standards.

quiz.q: What test does Iowa use for worker classification?
quiz.explanation: Iowa uses the Common law control test for worker classification.

laws.title: Child Labor Laws
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Labor Code — Restrictions on youth employment
laws.fullDescription: Iowa restricts employment of minors. Children under 14: very limited jobs only. Ages 14–15: restricted hours. Most minors under 18 need work permits. Standard child labor protections apply.
laws.penalty: Employers violating child labor laws: fines up to $10000 per violation.
laws.exceptions: Family farms and limited entertainment work have exemptions.

quiz.q: At what age do minors generally need work permits in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Most Iowa minors under 18 need work permits for regular employment.

laws.title: Equal Pay Act
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Civil Rights Code — Equal pay for equal work
laws.fullDescription: Iowa prohibits pay discrimination based on sex for substantially equal work. Equal pay laws prohibit sex-based wage discrimination.
laws.penalty: Back pay, compensatory damages, and attorney fees for violations.
laws.exceptions: Pay differences justified by seniority, merit, or non-sex factors are permitted.

quiz.q: What agency enforces equal pay laws in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa's civil rights agency and the federal EEOC both enforce equal pay laws.

laws.title: Anti-Discrimination in Employment
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Civil Rights Code — Protected classes in Iowa
laws.fullDescription: Iowa prohibits employment discrimination based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, age (40+), and disability. Standard protected classes.
laws.penalty: Compensatory damages, back pay, reinstatement, and attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Religious organizations may have limited exemptions for certain positions.

quiz.q: How many employees must an Iowa employer have before anti-discrimination laws apply?
quiz.explanation: Iowa anti-discrimination laws apply to employers with 15 or more employees.

laws.title: Landlord Entry Notice Requirement
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Landlord-Tenant Act — 24-hour notice required
laws.fullDescription: Iowa landlords must give tenants 24 hours' written notice before entering for non-emergency purposes. Entry at reasonable times.
laws.penalty: Unlawful entry may entitle tenant to damages or lease termination.
laws.exceptions: Emergencies (fire, flood, imminent harm) allow immediate entry without notice.

quiz.q: How many hours notice must Iowa landlords give before entering?
quiz.explanation: Iowa landlords must give 24 hours' notice before non-emergency entry.

laws.title: Security Deposit Rules
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Landlord-Tenant Act — Two months' rent maximum deposit
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Maximum security deposit is Two months' rent. Deposits must be returned within 30 days of move-out with an itemized statement of deductions.
laws.penalty: Landlord who wrongfully withholds deposit may owe double damages plus attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Deposits for pets may be separate in some cases.

quiz.q: How many days does a Iowa landlord have to return a security deposit?
quiz.explanation: Iowa landlords have 30 days to return security deposits after move-out.

laws.title: Rent Control Status — Not Statewide
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Housing Code — No statewide rent control
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Iowa prohibits local rent control ordinances.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a policy/regulatory matter.
laws.exceptions: Federally subsidized housing has separate rent rules.

quiz.q: Does Iowa have statewide rent control?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Iowa preempts local rent control.

laws.title: Eviction Process & Tenant Protections
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Landlord-Tenant Act — Notice and court process required
laws.fullDescription: Iowa landlords must provide: 5 days notice for nonpayment; 10 days for violations; 30 days for no-cause termination. Court filing required after notice expires.
laws.penalty: Self-help eviction (changing locks, removing belongings) is illegal.
laws.exceptions: Emergency situations may allow expedited proceedings.

quiz.q: How many days notice for non-payment of rent before eviction in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa requires 5 days notice for nonpayment of rent before filing for eviction.

laws.title: Short-Term Rental (STR) Regulations
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Regulated locally
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: STR regulations vary by municipality.

laws.exceptions: Owner-occupied properties renting a single room may have reduced requirements.

quiz.q: Are short-term rentals (Airbnb) regulated in Iowa?

laws.title: Property Tax
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Average 1.50% effective rate
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Average effective property tax rate is approximately 1.50%. Property taxes fund local services.
laws.penalty: Delinquent taxes accrue interest and may result in tax lien or foreclosure.
laws.exceptions: Senior citizens and disabled veterans often receive exemptions. Senior and veteran exemptions available.

quiz.q: What is the approximate average effective property tax rate in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa's average effective property tax rate is approximately 1.50%.

laws.title: Homestead Exemption
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Property Code — $25,000 assessed value reduction homestead exemption
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Homestead exemption reduces taxable value.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a protection for homeowners.

quiz.q: What is Iowa's homestead exemption?
quiz.explanation: Iowa's homestead exemption is $25,000 assessed value reduction.

laws.title: State Income Tax — Yes — flat 3.8% (phased in)
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §422.5 — Yes — flat 3.8% (phased in)
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Iowa is phasing in a flat 3.8% income tax by 2026, down from a complicated graduated system.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: civil penalties, back taxes, and possible criminal charges.

quiz.q: Does Iowa have a state income tax?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Iowa is transitioning to a flat 3.8% income tax.

laws.title: Sales Tax Rate
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Revenue Code — 6.0% statewide sales tax
laws.fullDescription: Iowa has a 6.0% statewide sales tax. Local taxes add to state rate. Combined state and local rates average 7.0%.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: civil penalties and criminal charges for substantial violations.
laws.exceptions: Exempt items typically include: Prescription drugs and groceries..

quiz.q: What is the statewide sales tax rate in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa's statewide sales tax is 6.0%.

laws.title: Estate / Inheritance Tax — No
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Revenue Code — No estate tax
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Iowa is phasing out its inheritance tax, to be fully eliminated by 2025.
laws.penalty: N/A — federal estate tax applies to all US residents with large estates.
laws.exceptions: Federal estate tax applies to estates over $13 million (2024).

quiz.q: Does Iowa have a state estate or inheritance tax?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Iowa is eliminating its inheritance tax.

laws.title: Smoke-Free Workplace Law
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Health Code — Clean Air Act / Smoke-Free law
laws.fullDescription: Iowa prohibits smoking in enclosed workplaces and public places.
laws.penalty: Violation: $100–$500 per incident for individuals.
laws.exceptions: Some private clubs and outdoor areas may be exempt.

quiz.q: Is smoking banned in workplaces and restaurants in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Comprehensive smoke-free law.

laws.title: Motorcycle Helmet Law
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §321.445 — Universal helmet law
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Iowa requires helmets only for motorcycle riders under 18.
laws.penalty: Helmet violation: $100 fine.
laws.exceptions: Adults 18+ exempt.

quiz.q: Who must wear a motorcycle helmet in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Iowa requires helmets for riders under 18 only.

laws.title: Seatbelt Law
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Vehicle Code — Mandatory seatbelts
laws.fullDescription: Iowa requires all front-seat occupants to wear seatbelts. Children under 8 or under 60 lbs must be in child safety seats.
laws.penalty: $25 fine for violations; higher for child restraint violations.
laws.exceptions: Some commercial vehicles and emergency situations may have limited exemptions.

quiz.q: Is the seatbelt law a primary offense in Iowa?
options: Yes, police can stop for seatbelt alone
quiz.explanation: Iowa's seatbelt law is a primary enforcement offense.

laws.title: Speed Limits
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Vehicle Code — Statutory speed limits
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Residential: 25 mph; highways: 65 mph; interstates: 70 mph; school zones: 20 mph. Posted limits vary by road.
laws.penalty: Speeding fines start at $50 and increase with severity; reckless driving is a criminal charge.
laws.exceptions: Emergency vehicles are exempt when responding.

quiz.q: What is the interstate speed limit in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa's standard interstate speed limit is 70 mph.

laws.title: Texting While Driving
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Vehicle Code — Texting banned while driving
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Texting while driving is prohibited.
laws.penalty: First offense: $50; repeat: $100.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are permitted while driving.

quiz.q: Is texting while driving banned in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Texting while driving is banned.

laws.title: DUI Checkpoint Legality
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Vehicle Code — Sobriety checkpoints permitted
laws.fullDescription: DUI sobriety checkpoints are legal in Iowa. DUI checkpoints legal with proper procedures.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines when checkpoints are legal.
laws.exceptions: Checkpoints must follow established procedures to be constitutional.

quiz.q: Are DUI sobriety checkpoints legal in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: DUI checkpoints are legal with proper procedures.

laws.title: Move Over Law
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Vehicle Code — Slow or move over for emergency vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Iowa's Move Over Law requires drivers to change lanes or slow down when passing stopped emergency vehicles and tow trucks and highway workers with flashing lights on the roadway or shoulder.
laws.penalty: Violation: $250 fine; if injury or death results, criminal charges may apply.
laws.exceptions: Required only when safe to do so without creating greater hazard.

quiz.q: Does Iowa's Move Over Law cover tow trucks?
quiz.explanation: Iowa's Move Over Law covers tow trucks.

laws.title: Cell Phone Use While Driving
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Traffic Code — Handheld device restrictions
laws.fullDescription: Beyond texting, Iowa restricts handheld phone use while driving.
laws.penalty: Fines range from $50 to $200.
laws.exceptions: Hands-free calls and navigation use are generally permitted.

quiz.q: Can drivers make calls on a handheld phone while driving in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Handheld restrictions while driving.

laws.title: Age of Majority
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Civil Code — Age 18 is legal adulthood
laws.fullDescription: In Iowa, the age of majority is 18. At 18, residents gain the right to vote, enter contracts, and make their own legal decisions. Age-specific restrictions still apply.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines civil rights.
laws.exceptions: Some rights have higher age thresholds: alcohol (21), cannabis where legal (21).

quiz.q: What is the age of majority in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa's age of majority is 18, consistent with most US states.

laws.title: Voting Rights & Restoration
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Election Code — Voter eligibility and felon restoration
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Felons lose voting rights during incarceration; restoration varies.
laws.penalty: Voting while ineligible (while incarcerated): criminal charge.
laws.exceptions: Mentally incapacitated persons adjudicated incompetent may lose voting rights.

quiz.q: When are voting rights restored to a felon in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Voting rights restored after sentence.

laws.title: Jury Duty Requirements
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Court Rules — Jury service
laws.fullDescription: Iowa citizens who are US citizens, 18+, registered voters (or driver's license holders) may be called for jury duty. Jurors receive $50/day. Employers must allow employees to serve.
laws.penalty: Willfully ignoring a jury summons: contempt of court, fines up to $500.
laws.exceptions: Exemptions include active military, police, extreme hardship, and some medical conditions.

quiz.q: What is the daily pay for jurors in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa jurors receive $50 per day for service.

laws.title: Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Child Welfare Act — Mandatory reporters
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Designated professionals are mandatory reporters. Reports must be made to child protective services or law enforcement. Good-faith reporters are protected from liability.
laws.penalty: Failure to report known child abuse: misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Attorney-client privilege may apply in limited circumstances.

quiz.q: Who must report suspected child abuse in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Designated professionals must report child abuse.

laws.title: Age of Consent
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Criminal Code — Age of consent is 16
laws.fullDescription: Iowa's age of consent is 16. Sexual activity with persons below the age of consent is a crime. Sex offenders must register with the state registry.
laws.penalty: Sexual abuse of a minor: Felony with sex offender registration..
laws.exceptions: Romeo and Juliet provision: Romeo and Juliet provision may apply..

quiz.q: What is the age of consent in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa's age of consent is 16.

laws.title: Emancipation of Minors
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Family Code — Court-ordered emancipation
laws.fullDescription: Iowa allows minors aged 16+ to petition for emancipation, granting adult legal status. The court considers whether it's in the minor's best interests and whether the minor can support themselves.
laws.penalty: N/A — emancipation is a civil court process.
laws.exceptions: Emancipation does not override minimum age laws for alcohol, cannabis, or voting.

quiz.q: At what minimum age can a minor petition for emancipation in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa allows minors aged 16+ to petition for emancipation.

laws.title: Curfew Laws for Minors

laws.fullDescription: Iowa: No statewide curfew; municipalities set rules.
laws.penalty: Curfew violation: minor taken into custody and released to parents; parents may face fines.

quiz.q: Does Iowa have a statewide youth curfew?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Curfews set locally.

laws.title: Corporal Punishment in Schools
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Education Code — Corporal punishment prohibited
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Corporal punishment is technically permitted in Iowa but rarely used in most districts.
laws.penalty: Educators using prohibited corporal punishment face administrative discipline and potential criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Physical restraint to prevent imminent harm is permitted.

quiz.q: Is corporal punishment allowed in Iowa public schools?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Corporal punishment is permitted but rarely used in Iowa schools.

laws.title: Homeschooling Regulations
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Education Code — Homeschooling requirements
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Families must notify district and cover required subjects.
laws.penalty: Failure to provide required education: mandatory enrollment in public school.
laws.exceptions: Some states have additional oversight or assessment requirements.

quiz.q: Does Iowa have strict homeschooling regulations?
quiz.explanation: Iowa has moderate-regulation homeschooling with moderate requirements.

laws.title: School Vaccination Requirements
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Health Code — Required vaccinations for school entry
laws.fullDescription: Iowa requires students to be vaccinated against standard childhood diseases for school entry. Standard vaccinations required for school entry.
laws.penalty: Unvaccinated students without exemptions may be excluded from school.
laws.exceptions: Exemptions available: medical and religious exemptions.

quiz.q: Can Iowa parents claim a philosophical exemption from school vaccinations?
quiz.explanation: Iowa vaccination exemptions: medical and religious exemptions.

laws.title: Abortion Laws
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §146B.2 — 6-week ban
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Iowa passed a 6-week abortion ban (fetal heartbeat law) that took effect in 2023 after the Iowa Supreme Court removed constitutional protections.
laws.penalty: Performing illegal abortion: felony.
laws.exceptions: Medical emergencies to save the life of the mother are typically exempt.

quiz.q: What is the gestational limit on abortion in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Iowa bans abortion after a fetal heartbeat is detectable (~6 weeks).

laws.title: Death Penalty — Authorized
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Criminal Code — Death penalty status
laws.fullDescription: Iowa has the death penalty. Iowa has the death penalty authorized but has not carried out an execution since 1963.
laws.penalty: Death penalty crimes: Capital murder.
laws.exceptions: Federal death penalty may apply to federal crimes regardless of state law.

quiz.q: Does Iowa have the death penalty?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Iowa has authorized the death penalty but has effectively maintained a moratorium since 1963.

laws.title: Medical Aid in Dying (MAID)
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Criminal Code — Assisted suicide illegal
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Medical aid in dying not legal.
laws.penalty: Assisting suicide: felony.
laws.exceptions: Withdrawal of life support and palliative sedation are legal with patient consent everywhere.

quiz.q: Is medical aid in dying (assisted suicide) legal in Iowa?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Medical aid in dying not legal.

laws.title: Drug Penalties (Non-Cannabis)
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Controlled Substances Act — Controlled Substances Act
laws.fullDescription: Iowa controlled substance penalties: Drug penalties follow state scheduling.

laws.exceptions: Prescribed medications used as directed are exempt.

quiz.q: Is simple drug possession a felony in Iowa?

laws.title: Asset Forfeiture Laws

laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Civil asset forfeiture permitted.

laws.title: Expungement & Record Sealing
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Criminal Code — Expungement availability
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Record sealing or expungement available for eligible offenses.

quiz.q: Can first-time non-violent offenders expunge their records in Iowa?

laws.title: Solitary Confinement Restrictions
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Corrections Code — Restricted housing policies
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: DOC policies limit solitary confinement.

quiz.q: Has Iowa restricted the use of solitary confinement?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Limited solitary confinement reforms.

laws.title: Private Prison Use
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Corrections Code — Private correctional facilities
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Some private facilities used.

quiz.q: Does Iowa use privately operated prisons?

laws.title: Police Body Camera Requirements
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Law Enforcement Code — Body camera law
laws.fullDescription: Iowa: Body camera policies vary by department.

quiz.q: Does Iowa have a statewide body camera law?
quiz.explanation: Iowa: Body camera policies vary.

laws.title: Red Flag Law (ERPO) — No

laws.fullDescription: Iowa does not have a Red Flag (ERPO) law. No Red Flag law.

laws.title: Hate Crime Laws

laws.fullDescription: Iowa has hate crime sentencing enhancements.

laws.title: Domestic Violence Laws & Protections
laws.subtitle: Iowa Code §Domestic Violence Act — Domestic Violence Act
